claims.result: Thermally, the filament and all fibers except f2 and f4 are supercritical; with the observed H13CO+ dispersion the turbulent critical mass exceeds the fiber line masses (except f3)
claims.finding: Fibers are supercritical if only thermal support applies, consistent with condensation formation; the turbulent discrepancy is attributed to feedback

evidence.loc: 3.4 Stability of the IRS 17 filament and fibers
evidence.quote: Compared with the observed line mass, the IRS 17 filament and all the fibers except f 2 and f 4 are thermally supercritical

evidence.loc: 3.4 Stability of the IRS 17 filament and fibers
evidence.quote: This contradicts the observed scenario of gravitational collapse of the fibers and the formation of the detected condensations within them.

claims.hypothesis: Are the condensations gravitationally bound and potential seeds of star formation?
claims.experiment: Virial parameter from thermal sound speed and condensation mass and radius; association with YSOs and outflows
claims.result: 25 of 30 condensations have alpha_vir <= 2 with median 1.1; two host Class I/0 YSOs and seven are associated with outflows
claims.finding: Most condensations are gravitationally bound and could seed star formation unless supported by magnetic fields

evidence.quote: This implies that most of identified condensations within the IRS 17 region are gravitationally bound and will undergo collapse unless supported by magnetic field.

claims.hypothesis: Does fragmentation proceed hierarchically from filament to fibers to condensations?
claims.experiment: Compare core spacing at filament scale (3 mm) and fiber scale (1.3 mm) with the linear cylinder model
claims.result: Random spacing at filament scale, periodic spacing within fertile fibers
claims.finding: There may be an intermediate fragmentation step involving fibers before core formation

evidence.quote: In other words, there may be an intermediate fragmentation step, involving the formation of fibers, before core formation out of the IRS 17 filament.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single assumed dust temperature (25 K) for filament, fibers and condensations drives all masses, line masses, densities and virial parameters, and no uncertainty on T is propagated
Condensation count differs between Sect. 3.2 (30) and abstract/summary (29)
Statistical significance of periodic spacing from only four fertile fibers with a few condensations each is not tested against random or non-periodic spacing

Velocity dispersion from H13CO+ at 1.8'' x 1.4'' is mismatched in resolution to 0.34'' fibers and condensations, so turbulent support at fiber scale is inferred from a scaling relation rather than measured
Fiber identification from continuum only with extraction parameters unstated, so reproducibility of the fiber and condensation lists is uncertain

missing_for_reproduction: QUARKS imaging parameters and continuum channel selection
Calibrated 1.3-mm and 3-mm images or recipe from the survey papers
Fiber-to-condensation association rule and H13CO+ moment-map recipe
Archive public status of the projects is not stated in the paper
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 100-300 GB raw for ATOMS 12-m+ACA and QUARKS 12-m+ACA execution blocks, if reprocessed; far less if survey image products are used (judgement, not from paper)
reproducibility.score_reason: Scale 1-5. Main numbers are tabulated and the stability and fragmentation steps are simple formulae, but imaging and extraction parameters are deferred to survey papers or unstated and archive release is not mentioned.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Paper does not state that the data are public and the getsf/SExtractor settings and QUARKS imaging parameters needed to redo the recipe are missing, although the results are numeric.
